ei.title: Theories and Practices of Sports Fandom
ei.subject: 영어2

fullPassage: Playing sports is one of the most common hobbies, but people also love to watch live sports games. If you go to any sports stadium, you will be able to find fans cheering wildly, crying with joy. In the case of football, some famous matches are accompanied by extreme fans, whose overly aggressive support of their team sometimes leads to confrontations with fans from opposition teams. If someone’s joy, sadness, and even anger emerge from the love of their team, what makes them so loyal? What does it mean for an individual to be a sports fan? And would their passion and cheering actually influence the performance of their team? These questions can be addressed from both an evolutionary and a social psychological perspective. From an evolutionary perspective, sports fandom emerged from our tribal hunter-gatherer ancestors tens of thousands of years ago. At that time, a person was far more likely to survive as a member of a group than as an isolated individual. People could help each other in groups when dealing with difficult tasks, such as carrying hunted animals that were too heavy for one person to handle. This mutual cooperation built trust and fostered relationships among group members. In fact, group membership was so important that tribes with a stronger sense of community were likely to defeat tribes whose members were less closely allied. Because of this, community membership was a survival mechanism for our ancestors, and the instinct to find one’s own tribe or group has been passed down to modern people. This may be how community membership influences our choice of a sports team and our sense of loyalty to that team. There are also two social psychological theories that might explain why we cheer for a sports team: optimal distinctiveness and basking in reflected glory. Though it may be human nature to form a group and feel a sense of belonging to that group, being a fan of a sports team is different from just having friends. Optimal distinctiveness theory states that everyone has a need for inclusion and differentiation. That is, individuals want to be included somewhere, but they also want to be different and unique. These two basic but competing needs can be satisfied through group membership. Sports team supporters are one such group. For example, if you are a fan of a football team based in your city, you can satisfy your need for inclusion by supporting the same team with other in-group members. This can also make you feel unique because your team’s fans are different from the fans of other teams. This feeling of uniqueness is reinforced by sports teams’ deliberate use of their team colors and songs. Another explanation for sports fandom is a phenomenon called “basking in reflected glory.” This means that you feel successful by associating yourself with others’ success, especially when you are connected to them in some way. This phenomenon is closely related to people’s love for their sports teams. People feel proud when their team wins the game or performs well. Even though a team’s triumph may not offer its fans any immediate benefits, the mere act of watching the game brings them satisfaction. This connection with sports teams can sometimes grow so strong among some passionate supporters that they even identify themselves with their teams. Because of this identification, they often consider criticism toward their team as a personal attack and become violent in extreme cases. However, as long as the behavior of sports fans does not go too far and harm others, cheering can become a means for them to express their emotions. Supporting a team passionately can help people forget about their daily life challenges. It can also have positive effects on our brains. For instance, when you cheer for a team and your team wins the game, your brain may release dopamine. Dopamine, a chemical known as the “happy hormone,” makes you feel pleasure when you reach a goal. If you have pursued the goal for a long time, the effect is greater. So it is a particular thrill when a team achieves victory following a series of back-to-back losses. While you are cheering, your brain may also release oxytocin, a hormone that contributes to feelings of bonding between people. Sports fandom brings benefits not only to individual fans but also to the performance of sports teams. When a team competes in their home stadium, their fans gather to watch the game. Typically, the cheers from the home team’s fans are louder than those from the visiting team’s supporters. This dynamic has an impact on the performance of the home team, as confirmed by a study in 2021. The study examined the relationship between cheering and goals scored in matches. It compared home matches in an Italian football league from 2013 to 2019 with matches during the pandemic when crowds were banned from entering stadiums. It was found that the home team’s performance decreased by eight percent on average without crowds. This means that cheering helps the team’s performance to some extent, although it may not be the determining factor. Sports fandom can be analyzed using both evolutionary and social psychological approaches. Through these perspectives, we can understand why people have loyalty and support for their teams. Given that sports fandom has become more and more common in modern times, we should think about our role as fans. We should establish a healthy culture of fandom and seek ways to practice fandom that can have a positive influence on society.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ contribute → contributes: 관계대명사 that의 선행사가 a hormone(단수)이므로 contributes
det.analysis:
✅ ① release: 조동사 may 뒤에 동사원형 release가 와서 'may release(분비할 수 있다)'로 적절
✅ ② reach: 'when you reach a goal(목표에 도달할 때)'에서 주어 you에 맞는 현재형 동사로 적절
✅ ③ pursued: 'If you have pursued the goal'에서 현재완료(have p.p.)를 이루는 과거분사로 적절
❌ ④ contribute → contributes: 'a hormone that ___ to feelings of bonding'에서 관계대명사 that이 가리키는 선행사는 a hormone(호르몬, 단수)이다. 단수 주어에는 contributes를 써야 한다 ← 정답
det.tip: 관계대명사 that의 선행사가 단수(a hormone)이면 동사도 단수(contributes)

det.korean: ② could helped → could help: 조동사 could 뒤에는 동사원형 help

det.korean: 홈 이점에 관한 2021년 연구.
det.analysis:
① 본문 'the cheers from the home team's fans are louder than those from the visiting team's supporters'에서 '홈 팀' 팬의 함성이 더 크므로 불일치
② 본문 'It compared home matches ~ from 2013 to 2019 with matches during the pandemic'에서 팬데믹 기간 경기와도 비교했으므로 '~만 분석했다'는 불일치
③ 본문 'the home team's performance decreased by eight percent on average without crowds'와 일치 ← 정답
④ 본문 'it may not be the determining factor'에서 응원이 '결정적 요인은 아닐 수 있다'고 했으므로 '유일한 요인'은 불일치
det.tip: 숫자·대상(홈 팀, 8퍼센트, 결정적 요인 아님)을 정확히 대조하세요.

ch: 원정 팀 팬들의 함성이 홈 팀 팬들의 함성보다 대체로 더 크다.
관중이 없을 때 홈 팀의 경기력은 평균 8퍼센트 감소했다.
응원은 팀의 성과를 결정짓는 유일한 요인으로 밝혀졌다.

questions.passage: Optimal distinctiveness theory ①<u>states</u> that everyone has a need for inclusion and differentiation. That is, individuals want to be ②<u>included</u> somewhere, but they also want to be different and unique. These two basic but competing needs ③<u>can</u> be satisfied through group membership. For example, if you are a fan of a football team based in your city, you can satisfy your need for inclusion by ④<u>support</u> the same team with other in-group members.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ support → supporting: 전치사 by 뒤에는 동명사(-ing)
det.analysis:
✅ ① states: 주어 'Optimal distinctiveness theory(단수)'에 맞는 현재형 동사로 적절
✅ ② included: 'want to be included somewhere'에서 '속하게 되고 싶다'는 수동의 의미이므로 to be + 과거분사로 적절
✅ ③ can: 'These two ~ needs can be satisfied'에서 조동사로 뒤의 be satisfied와 어울려 적절
❌ ④ support → supporting: 'satisfy your need for inclusion by ___ the same team'에서 by는 전치사이므로 뒤에 동명사(-ing)가 와야 한다. 따라서 supporting이 맞다 ← 정답
det.tip: by + 동명사(supporting): ~함으로써

questions.passage: It can also have positive effects on our brains.  For instance, when you cheer for a team and your team wins the game, your brain may release dopamine.  Dopamine, a chemical known as the “happy hormone,” makes you feel pleasure when you reach a goal.  If you have pursued the goal for a long time, the effect is greater.  So it is a particular thrill when a team achieves victory following a series of back-to-back losses.  While you are cheering, your brain may also release oxytocin, a hormone that contributes to feelings of bonding between people.
questions.stem: 위 글에 따르면, 응원하는 팀이 경기에서 이겼을 때 뇌가 분비할 수 있는, '행복 호르몬(happy hormone)'이라 불리는 화학 물질의 이름을 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (1단어, 영어로)

det.korean: 행복 호르몬으로 불리는 화학 물질.
det.analysis: 본문 'your brain may release dopamine. Dopamine, a chemical known as the "happy hormone," makes you feel pleasure when you reach a goal.'에서 팀이 이겼을 때 뇌가 분비하며 '행복 호르몬'으로 불리는 화학 물질은 dopamine(도파민)이다.
det.tip: known as the "happy hormone"(행복 호르몬으로 불리는)에서 dopamine을 찾습니다.

questions.passage: There are also two social psychological theories that might explain why we cheer for a sports team: optimal distinctiveness and basking in reflected glory.  Though it may be human nature to form a group and feel a sense of belonging to that group, being a fan of a sports team is different from just having friends.  Optimal distinctiveness theory states that everyone has a need for inclusion and differentiation.  That is, individuals want to be included somewhere, but they also want to be different and unique.  These two basic but competing needs can be satisfied through group membership.  Sports team supporters are one such group.  For example, if you are a fan of a football team based in your city, you can satisfy your need for inclusion by supporting the same team with other in-group members.  This can also make you feel unique because your team’s fans are different from the fans of other teams.  This feeling of uniqueness is reinforced by sports teams’ deliberate use of their team colors and songs.  Another explanation for sports fandom is a phenomenon called “basking in reflected glory.
questions.stem: 위 글에 따르면, 최적 독특성 이론과 함께 우리가 스포츠 팀을 응원하는 이유를 설명하는 또 하나의 현상을 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (4단어, 영어로)

det.korean: 팬덤을 설명하는 두 번째 사회심리 현상.
det.analysis: 본문 'two social psychological theories that might explain why we cheer for a sports team: optimal distinctiveness and basking in reflected glory.'와 'Another explanation for sports fandom is a phenomenon called "basking in reflected glory."'에서, 최적 독특성과 함께 언급되는 또 하나의 현상은 basking in reflected glory(반사된 영광 누리기)이다.
det.tip: optimal distinctiveness와 짝을 이루는 basking in reflected glory(네 단어)를 찾습니다.

questions.passage: This connection with sports teams can sometimes grow so strong that some supporters even identify themselves with their teams. Because of this identification, they often consider __________ (criticize) toward their team as a personal attack.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 흐름에 맞도록 괄호 안에 주어진 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어, 영어로)

det.korean: criticism: 동사 consider의 목적어 자리이므로 명사형
det.analysis: 구문 분석: 'they often consider ___ toward their team as a personal attack'에서 동사 consider의 목적어 자리이므로 명사가 필요하다. 동사 criticize(비판하다)의 명사형은 criticism(비판)이다. 'consider A as B(A를 B로 여기다)' 구조에서 A 자리에 온다.
det.tip: criticize(동사) → criticism(명사): 비판

questions.passage: Playing sports is one of the most common hobbies, but people also love to watch live sports games.  If you go to any sports stadium, you will be able to find fans cheering wildly, crying with joy.  In the case of football, some famous matches are accompanied by extreme fans, whose overly aggressive support of their team sometimes leads to confrontations with fans from opposition teams.  If someone’s joy, sadness, and even anger emerge from the love of their team, what makes them so loyal?  What does it mean for an individual to be a sports fan?  And would their passion and cheering actually influence the performance of their team?  These questions can be addressed from both an evolutionary and a social psychological perspective.  From an evolutionary perspective, sports fandom emerged from our tribal hunter-gatherer ancestors tens of thousands of years ago.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 글 전체를 아우르는 중심 소재.
det.analysis:
① 글은 스포츠 팬덤을 진화적·사회심리학적 관점으로 설명하고, 마지막에 건강한 응원 문화를 세우자고 제안하므로 글 전체를 포괄하는 주제 ← 정답
② 극단적 팬의 폭력은 일부 내용일 뿐 전체 주제가 아님
③ 도파민·옥시토신은 뇌에 미치는 긍정적 효과의 예시일 뿐 전체 주제가 아님
④ 관중 수와 입장권 수익은 본문에서 다루지 않음
det.tip: 주제는 글 전체(진화적·사회심리학적 관점 + 건강한 팬덤)를 포괄해야 합니다.

ch: 스포츠 팬덤을 진화적·사회심리학적 관점에서 이해하고 건강한 응원 문화를 모색하기
축구 경기에서 극단적인 팬들이 일으키는 폭력 사태와 그 처벌 방안
도파민과 옥시토신이 인간의 뇌 건강에 미치는 의학적 효능
홈경기장 관중 수가 구단의 입장권 판매 수익에 미치는 영향

questions.passage: Playing sports is one of the most common hobbies, but people also love to watch live sports games.  If you go to any sports stadium, you will be able to find fans cheering wildly, crying with joy.  In the case of football, some famous matches are accompanied by extreme fans, whose overly aggressive support of their team sometimes leads to confrontations with fans from opposition teams.  If someone’s joy, sadness, and even anger emerge from the love of their team, what makes them so loyal?  What does it mean for an individual to be a sports fan?  And would their passion and cheering actually influence the performance of their team?  These questions can be addressed from both an evolutionary and a social psychological perspective.  From an evolutionary perspective, sports fandom emerged from our tribal hunter-gatherer ancestors tens of thousands of years ago.
questions.stem: 위 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 글쓴이가 전하려는 핵심 메시지.
det.analysis:
① 본문 'a team's triumph may not offer its fans any immediate benefits'에서 즉각적 이득은 없다고 했으므로 요지와 반대
② 본문 'it may not be the determining factor'에서 유일한 요인이 아니라고 했으므로 반대
③ 팬덤의 진화적·사회심리학적 뿌리를 설명하고 건강한 응원 문화를 실천하자는 결론과 정확히 통하는 핵심 메시지 ← 정답
④ 본문 'Sports fandom brings benefits not only to individual fans but also to the performance of sports teams'에서 팀 성과에도 영향을 준다고 했으므로 반대
det.tip: 요지는 글쓴이의 핵심 주장(뿌리 이해 + 건강한 팬덤 실천)입니다.

ch: 스포츠 팬은 팀의 승리에서 즉각적인 금전적 이득을 얻는다.
응원은 팀의 경기력을 결정짓는 유일하고 확실한 요인이다.
스포츠 팬덤은 진화적·사회심리학적 뿌리를 가지며, 팬은 건강한 방식으로 응원 문화를 실천해야 한다.
팬덤은 개인에게만 이로울 뿐 팀의 성과에는 전혀 영향을 주지 않는다.

questions.passage: This connection with sports teams can sometimes grow so strong among some passionate supporters that they even identify themselves with their teams.  Because of this identification, they often consider criticism toward their team as a personal attack and become violent in extreme cases.  However, as long as the behavior of sports fans does not go too far and harm others, __________.  Supporting a team passionately can help people forget about their daily life challenges.
questions.stem:
위 글의 내용을 바탕으로, 다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 조건에 따라 영작하시오. (영어로)

'응원은 그들이 자신의 감정을 표현하는 수단이 될 수 있다.'

[조건]
(1) a, become, can, cheering, emotions, express, for, means, their, them, to를 모두 사용할 것
(2) 정확히 11단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: cheering can become a means for them to express their emotions
det.analysis:
구문 분석:
- cheering(주어) + can become(동사): 응원은 ~이 될 수 있다
- a means(보어): 하나의 수단
- for them(전치사구): 그들을 위한 → to express their emotions로 이어짐
- to express their emotions(to부정사): 자신의 감정을 표현하는
- 순서대로 놓으면 cheering / can / become / a / means / for / them / to / express / their / emotions
det.tip: a means for + 목적격 + to부정사: ~가 …하는 수단 / cheering can become a means(응원은 수단이 될 수 있다)

questions.wa: cheering can become a means for them to express their emotions
accept: cheering can become a means for them to express their emotions
